chunks: He (peace be upon him) said when the news of the killing of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr reached him
Our grief over him is as great as their joy for it, except that they have lost an enemy and we have lost a friend.
ai.seo_question: What was Imam Ali's reaction to the death of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) articulates a profound theological symmetry in mourning, where the intensity of grief matches the joy of adversaries, yet distinguishes the loss by contrasting the removal of an 'enemy' with the loss of a 'beloved' (habib). This narration, found in *Nahj al-Balagha*, highlights the personal and communal cost of the Umayyad consolidation of power, framing Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr not merely as a political opponent but as a cherished companion whose death deepened the spiritual sorrow of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 325. When the news of killing of Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr [1] reached Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, he said:
Our grief over him is as great as their (i.e. the enemy’s) joy for it, except that they have lost an enemy and we have lost a friend.
